full_judgment:
A.K.M. Fazlur Rahman, J: These two Rules issued on two separate applications under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure are directed against the judgment and decree dated 17.8.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Mymensingh in other Class Appeal Nos. 373 and 374 of 1997 allowing both the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 29.9.1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Phulpur, Mymensingh decreeing other class suit No. 18 of 1993 and dismissing other class suit No. 19 of 1997 both for specific performance of contract for sale. Both the rules arisen out of the same judgment and decree have been heard together and are being disposed of by this judgment. 

 12. Zahura Khatoon was examined as D. W. 1 She said that she sold the suit land to Mohammad Ali for consideration of Tk. 40,000/- who paid her Taka. 35,000/- and she executed the bainapatra. It was agreed upon that one year after balance consideration of Tk. 5000/- would be paid. But Mohammad Ali did not pay the amount. For that she had told him that she would not give him the land. Later on Mohammad Ali filed the case. Then salishi was held by the village headmen. Mohammad Ali gave her Tk. 5000/- and she tiled aposhnama wherein she put J. T. J. In terms of that aposhnama Mohammad Ali would get decree. He denied the suggestion that she executed a binapatra in favour of Nazrul Islam that the bainapatra in favour of Mohammad Ali was without consideration or that the aposhnama was collusive. Mohammad Ali had possession in the land. Nazrul had no possession. Total area of the suit plot no. 271 was 8 katah 1 decimal of which 7 katah 1 decimal was sold to Mohammad Ali and 10 decimals was sold to Sayeb Ali. There was no talk of selling the same land to Nazrul. The possession of the land wasnot delivered to Nazrul. The bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was genuine. She did not execute bainapatra to Nazrul. In cross-examination by the defendant no. 2, Nazrul she admitted that Mohamtnad Ali was her brother as neighbour. She went to the sub-Registrar office for registration of a deed of sale in favour of Mohammad Ali, but due to absence of the sub-Registrar such deed could not be registered. She could not say whether she filed written statement in other Class suit No. 18 of 1993 filed by Nazrul. She denied The suggestion that she sold the land to Nazrul for consideration of Tk. 30,000/-and on receipt of Tk. 26,000/- executed the bainapatrea and delivered him possession or that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was antedated or that no possession was delivered to Mohammad All and he had no possession. 

 17. The learned Senior Assistant Judge on consideration of the above evidence decreed Other Class Suit No. 18 of 1993 finding the bainapatra of Nazrul Islam genuine and dismissed Other Class Suit No. 19 of 1997 with the finding that the bainapatra of 'Mohammad Ali was collusive and attested. Being aggrieved by that judgment and decree Mohammad Ali preferred Other Class No. 373 of 1997 against the Judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 19 of 1997 and Other Class Appeal No. 374 of 1997 against the Judgment and decree passed in Other Class Suit No. 18 of 1993. Both the appears were heard analogously by the Subordinate Judge 2nd Court Mymensingh, who allowed both the appeals reversing the Judgment and decrees passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, in both the suit and thereby decreed other Class suit No. 19 of 1997 of Mohammad Ali and dismissed the Other Class Suit No. 18 of 1993 of Nazrul Islam. Against that Judgment and decree Nazrul Isalm moved this Court by filing two revisional applications under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained these two Rules. 

 18. Mr. Md. Hassan Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of petitioner Nazrul Islam in both the civil revisions, makes his submission supporting the Rules assailing the judgment and decrees passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in the appeals and supporting the judgment and decrees passed by the trial Court. He submits that the final Court on consideration of evidence both documentary and oral including the expert opinion came to correct finding that the bainapatra of petitioner, Nazrul Islam was genuine. The appellate court without discussing and considering the evidence adduced by petitioner, Nazrul and without refuting the findings of the trial Court most illegally dismissed other Class Suit No. 18 of 1993 and decreed other Class Suit No. 19 of 1997. He further submits that Nazrul specifically challenged the genuineness of bainapatra of Mohammad Ali and contended that after filing of his suit, Zahura Khatoon in order to deceive him in collusion with Mohammad Ali subsequently created the bainapatra, Exht.1, without consideration showing  its antendated execution. Mohammad Ali failed to prove that his bainaparta was genuine, To conceal the fact that the stamp papers of the bainapatra were purchased long after the date of execution of the bainapatra the bainapatra was taken back and false story of missing of the same was introduced. The Photostat copy of the bainapatra which was marked as Exbt. 2 is not the secondary evidence of the bainapatra as the back pages of the stamps on which the date of purchasing the stamp papers was written was not photostated. Moreover the photostat copy of the bainapatra was not proved in accordance with law and illegally admitted into evidence. Zahura Khatun some days after filing of the suit by Mohammad Ali apparent in the suit filed a written statement admitting the plaint case and conceded that she would execute and register the deed of sale if the balance consideration of Tk. 8,000/- would be paid to her. Her such conduct is not normal and usual Normally the defendant who would not like to contest the suit would not appear and file written statement admitting the plaint case spending money from his pocket. Such abnormal conduct of Jahura clearly indicate that in order to defeat the suit filed by Nazrul she in collusion with Mohammad Ali filed the suit creating an antedated bainapatra. The trial Court on consideration of these aspects rightly and legally dismissed the suit of Mohammad Ali and decreed the suit Nazrul, But the appellate Court without refuting the finding of the trial Court illegally decreed the suit of Mohammad Ali and dismissed that of Nazrul. Moreover the appellate Courts finding is not based on evidence and as such illegal occasioning failure of Justice. Hence the same warrants interference by this Court under section 115(1) of the civil procedure code. 

 19. Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Mohammad Ali, makes his submission opposing both the Rules and supporting the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate Court. He submits that the execution of bainapatra of Mohammad Ali is admitted by its executant Zahura Khatoon. Thus the bainapatra has been proved genuine. The Petitioner, Nazrul who claimed the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali collusive and antedated adduced no evidence in support of his such claim, neither he nor any one of his witnesses gave evidence that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was antedated one or it was collusively created subsequently showing its execution on an earlier date. He as D.W.2 simply said that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was false, collusive and not genuine. Thus he failed to prove that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was antedated and collusive. He further submits that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali being earlier one and admitted by its executant the appellate court rightly and legally decreed the suit of Mohammad Ali and dismissed that of Nazrul. There was no non-consideration or misreading of evidence and illegality occasioning failure of justice. So the impugned judgment and decree do not warrant interference by this court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 21. Moreover, Zahura Khatoon did not contest the suit filed by Nazrul by filing a written statement. She as D.W. 1 did not specifically deny the plaint case of Nazrul Islam therefore, the trial Court rightly and legally decreed the suit of Nazrul. The appellate Court without refuting such findings of facts of the trial Court and discussing the evidence adduced by Nazrul dismissed his suit reversion the finding of the trial Court, which is contrary to law. 

 22. Therefore the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court in other class Appeal No. 374 of 1997 arisen out of the other class suit No. 18 of 1993 being perverse occasioned failure of justice and as such the same warrant interference by this Court. 

 28. The trial court considering the above facts and circumstances rightly and legally held that the bainapatra of Mohammad Ali was antedated and collusive and accordingly dismissed his suit. Mohammad Ali failed to prove his alleged contract. The appellate court without refuting the above findings of the trial court gassed on evidence on record pointing some discrepancies and inconsistency in the oral testimonies of the witnesses reversed the judgment and decrees of the trial court. 

 29. On the above reasons I am of the view that the appellate court acted illegally in allowing both the appeals and thereby decreeing other class suit No. 19 of 1997 and dismissing the other class suit No. 18 of 1993. The impugned judgment and decree occasioned failure of justice and as such warrant interference by this court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 30. In the result, both the Rules are made absolute without any order as to the costs. The judgment and decree dated 17.8.2000 passed by the Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Mymensingh in Other Class Appeal Nos. 373 and 374 of 1997 reversing the judgment and decrees dated 29. 9. 1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Phulpur, Mymensingh in Other Class Suit Nos. 18 of 1993 and 19 of 1997 are hereby set aside and those of the trial court are restored.
